audits.title: Cesarean section rate changes after audit and feedback with the Ten Group Classification System in a French perinatal network: A retrospective pre-post study.
audits.standard: Robson Ten Group Classification System audit and feedback of caesarean section rates
audits.setting: French perinatal network of 10 maternity wards, Yvelines

cycle1.result: Overall caesarean section rate 24.5% (audit feedback of overall rates only).

audits.intervention: Audit and feedback providing caesarean section rates for each Robson group.

cycle2.result: Overall caesarean section rate 25.1%; no significant difference in any Robson group after adjustment.

audits.other_findings: Audit did not reduce variability of caesarean rates between maternity wards.
audits.citation: Quibel T, Chesnais M, Bouyer C, Rozenberg P, Bouyer J. Cesarean section rate changes after audit and feedback with the Ten Group Classification System in a French perinatal network: A retrospective pre-post study. Acta Obstet Gynecol Scand. 2022;101(4):388-395. doi:10.1111/aogs.14327. PMID: 35277968.

audits.title: Application of the Robson classification in assessing cesarean section rates: an audit of a tertiary care hospital's gynecology department in Karachi, Pakistan.
audits.standard: WHO recommendation that caesarean rates not exceed 10-15%; Robson Ten Group Classification
audits.setting: Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Holy Family Hospital, Karachi; tertiary care hospital

cycle1.result: 507 caesarean sections among 1464 deliveries; main contributors group 5 (51.9%), group 2 (18.5%) and group 10 (14.4%).

audits.other_findings: 48.8% elective and 51.2% emergency; leading indications previous caesarean (32.3%) and non-progress of labour (21.15%).
audits.citation: Abidi SMA, Hussain SNF, Abbas S, Abidi STF, Haresh S. Application of the Robson classification in assessing cesarean section rates: an audit of a tertiary care hospital's gynecology department in Karachi, Pakistan. Ther Adv Reprod Health. 2025;19:26334941251339710. doi:10.1177/26334941251339710. PMID: 40386352.

audits.title: Caesarean section in term nulliparous women at Wellington Hospital in 2001: a regional audit.
audits.standard: Standards from the literature for caesarean section indications and care

cycle1.result: Corrected CS rate 27%; elective 36/743 (5%), emergency 165/743 (22%); a significant proportion of CS did not meet the standards.

audits.other_findings: Commonest indications were dystocia (48%), suspected fetal compromise (23%) and malpresentation (20%).
audits.citation: Sangalli M, Guidera A. Caesarean section in term nulliparous women at Wellington Hospital in 2001: a regional audit. N Z Med J. 2004;117(1206):U1184. PMID: 15570353.

audits.title: Introducing caesarean section audit in a regional teaching hospital in The Netherlands.
audits.setting: The Haga hospital, regional teaching hospital, The Hague
audits.intervention: Caesarean section audit introduced into daily report meetings

cycle2.result: 228 caesarean sections in 1221 deliveries (18.7%), significantly lower; consensus on lack of necessity in 6.7%.

audits.other_findings: Assisted vaginal delivery, neonatal outcome and induction rates were comparable.
audits.citation: van Dillen J, Lim F, van Rijssel E. Introducing caesarean section audit in a regional teaching hospital in The Netherlands. Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol. 2008;139(2):151-156. doi:10.1016/j.ejogrb.2008.01.008. PMID: 18313198.

audits.title: [Introducing a daily obstetric audit: A solution to reduce the cesarean section rate?].
audits.standard: Daily audit of accuracy of caesarean indications
audits.setting: Obstetrics department, regional university teaching hospital (CHU de Grenoble)

cycle1.result: 248 caesareans in 947 deliveries (26.2%); emergency caesarean rate 19.6%; instrumental delivery rate 14.4%.

audits.intervention: Introduction of a daily obstetric audit of caesarean indications at the daily report meeting

cycle2.result: 246 caesareans in 1033 deliveries (23.8%), P=0.014; emergency caesarean rate 16.7%, P=0.02; instrumental delivery rate 17.2%, P=0.0004.

audits.other_findings: Maternal and neonatal health was unchanged between periods.
audits.citation: Lasnet A, Jelen AF, Douysset X, Pons JC, Sergent F. [Introducing a daily obstetric audit: A solution to reduce the cesarean section rate?]. J Gynecol Obstet Biol Reprod (Paris). 2015;44(6):550-557. doi:10.1016/j.jgyn.2014.08.003. PMID: 25260605.

audits.title: Reducing the Primary Cesarean Birth Rate: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.standard: National and state benchmark primary caesarean rates
audits.setting: Colorado community hospital and its largest maternity care provider group
audits.intervention: Reduced elective induction before 41 weeks, triage admission at 4 cm or more, intermittent auscultation, and monthly feedback of each obstetrician's caesarean rate.

cycle2.result: Primary caesarean birth rate 12.2% (57.8% decrease, OR 0.345).

audits.citation: Javernick JA, Dempsey A. Reducing the Primary Cesarean Birth Rate: A Quality Improvement Project. J Midwifery Womens Health. 2017;62(4):477-483. doi:10.1111/jmwh.12606. PMID: 28703927.

audits.title: Cesarean Audit Using Robson Classification at a Tertiary Care Center in Bihar: A Retrospective Study.
audits.standard: Ideal caesarean section rate 10% to 15%; Robson Ten Group Classification System
audits.setting: Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Indira Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences, Patna; tertiary care centre

cycle1.result: Caesarean section rate 38.16% (812/2128); Robson group 5 contributed 34.97%, group 2 26.35%, group 1 15.51%, group 10 7.14%.

audits.other_findings: Primary caesarean 61.82% vs repeat 38.17%; main indications previous CS, fetal distress, failed induction, arrest of labour, malpresentation.
audits.citation: Pravina P, Ranjana R, Goel N. Cesarean Audit Using Robson Classification at a Tertiary Care Center in Bihar: A Retrospective Study. Cureus. 2022;14(3):e23133. doi:10.7759/cureus.23133. PMID: 35425673.

audits.title: Safe Reduction of Nulliparous, Term, Singleton, Vertex Cesarean Delivery Rates Using Multidisciplinary Quality Improvement Efforts.
audits.standard: ACOG criteria for caesarean indications (failed induction, active-phase arrest, second-stage arrest, prelabour/scheduled caesarean); NTSV caesarean rate
audits.setting: Level IV urban academic centre, Texas Children's Hospital / Baylor College of Medicine, Houston
audits.intervention: Multidisciplinary workgroup; NTSV rates shared stratified by indication, physician and ethnicity; nurse audit of oxytocin protocol adherence; non-drug labour pain options; physician scorecards on NTSV rate and adherence to ACOG criteria.
audits.other_findings: Chart review of 298 NTSV caesareans (May-October 2023) found 13.8% did not meet ACOG criteria, most often failed induction (23.4%); severe newborn complications unchanged (0.5% vs 0.5%).
audits.citation: McGee C, Green CA, Shubert L, Babalola A, Timmins A, Gonzales-Hughes S, et al.. Safe Reduction of Nulliparous, Term, Singleton, Vertex Cesarean Delivery Rates Using Multidisciplinary Quality Improvement Efforts. O G Open. 2026;3(2):e157. doi:10.1097/og9.0000000000000157. PMID: 41821621.

audits.title: Influence of audit and feedback on use of caesarean section in a geographically-defined population.
audits.setting: Main hospital serving a geographically defined health district (85% of births)
audits.intervention: Three main reasons for the rising caesarean rate were fed back non-directively to resident obstetricians throughout 1986.

cycle2.result: Caesarean section rate 12.7% (P < 0.005); 12.2% in the informed hospital v 15.6% in other hospitals.

audits.other_findings: Most of the fall was due to fewer sections for the three indications that had driven the rise between 1974 and 1982.
audits.citation: Kiwanuka AI, Moore WM. Influence of audit and feedback on use of caesarean section in a geographically-defined population. Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol. 1993;50(1):59-64. doi:10.1016/0028-2243(93)90165-9. PMID: 8365537.

audits.title: Promoting effective care: Reducing primary cesarean births through team engagement and standardization of care at a community hospital.
audits.standard: Healthy People 2020 NTSV caesarean birth target of 23.9%
audits.intervention: Four PDSA cycles: team huddles using a best practices checklist for labour dystocia and abnormal fetal tracings, and audits of unplanned caesarean births.

cycle2.result: 13 of 55 NTSV patients had caesarean birth; rate 23.6%.

audits.other_findings: 53 huddles held by 218 staff for 28 patients; team engagement scores improved from 85% to 98%; mean effective care caesarean score 51%.
audits.citation: Wise G, Jolles D. Promoting effective care: Reducing primary cesarean births through team engagement and standardization of care at a community hospital. Nurs Forum. 2019;54(4):601-610. doi:10.1111/nuf.12384. PMID: 31523833.

cycle1.result: Overall caesarean section rate 36.7%; Group 5 group-specific rate 84.5%; referred 51.3% vs non-referred 30.3%; most common indication previous caesarean without trial of labour (28.9%).
